terms.comment: prōnōmen dēmōnstrātīvum: hic, ille (Traupman 224). Lewis & Short gives the word only in rhetoric (the oratory of praise and blame) and of the forefinger; we have not found the grammatical sense there. Varro calls hic and quis articulī (see article).

phrases.latin: Dā exempla prōnōminis dēmōnstrātīvī. — Hic, ille.
phrases.english: Give some examples of a demonstrative pronoun. — This one, that one.

demonstrativus.html: Vowels before ns are long (Cic. Or. 159), as in mōnstrum, dēmōnstrō.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): p. 224, p. 246.
